issues.subject: Second Reel · {date}: Night buses and a Sunday matinee
issues.text:
Second Reel · {date}

Night buses and a Sunday matinee

Listings for 19–25 October. The late Saturday show at Low Arch now starts twenty minutes earlier. Thursday's print is confirmed.

Thursday at Junction Hall: The Last Inspector
Sonia Baird's 1978 film spends most of its first reel following a bus conductor through the depot at Mile End. The surviving 16mm print has a small splice halfway through the stairwell scene. Projectionist Marion Cole is introducing it at 19:10. There are 58 seats, unreserved, and the front row is very close to the screen. Tickets are £8 on the door if any are left.
https://secondreel.example/listings/the-last-inspector-junction-hall

Saturday at Low Arch: After the Terminus
A double bill of two short features about people waiting for the first bus of the day. Len Ward's The Room Above the Cafe runs 49 minutes, followed by the recently subtitled Platform Two from Mette Hald. Doors are at 20:20, projector on at 20:40. The arch is cold once the audience sits down. If you're arriving late, the quieter door is on the yard side.
https://secondreel.example/listings/after-the-terminus-low-arch

Sunday at Clover Picture House: The Painted Pond
A 14:30 matinee of Ellis Venn's 1964 studio comedy about a groundskeeper caught repainting a municipal pond. It's from a digital restoration with all the original hand-lettered credits. The usher will leave the house lights low for the first five minutes and there's a short interval before the last reel. The foyer exhibition has the production designer's drawing of the pond mechanism, which is fun to inspect after.
https://secondreel.example/listings/the-painted-pond-clover

See you in the stalls,
Albie Morse, listings editor

Second Reel · 26 Wren Passage, London WC1N 3JF

issues.subject: Second Reel · {date}: Four reels from a vanished street
issues.text:
Second Reel · {date}

Four reels from a vanished street

There's a local history programme on the south side of the river and a dance film worth seeing from far enough back to get both dancers in view.

Wednesday at Lantern Rooms: Half the Street
Beryl Dent's film starts with a grocer chalking up the price of apples on the same board his father used. Ten years later the bus stop is the only thing still there. The Lantern has borrowed four reels from Dent's sister and pieced them together with a photocopy of the editor's running order. At 18:45 the archive team is showing the inspection notes before the screening proper.
https://secondreel.example/listings/half-the-street-lantern

Friday at Harrowgate Studio: Two Sets of Steps
Dance teacher Po Chan built his single-room film around two students learning a duet from opposite ends of a mirror. The image is nearly square. Sit about halfway back to get the effect of the whole floor coming into view near the end. The 21:00 print is on 35mm, with a replacement first leader spliced on for this run. Drinks can come in with you up to the bell.
https://secondreel.example/listings/two-sets-of-steps-harrowgate

Sunday at Clover: The Envelope House
A former sorting-office clerk has to tell a whole street that she has been keeping their post. It's a talky one, with the last conversation filmed in a single take in the sorting room. Clover is showing a 2K copy at 15:00 with descriptive captions. The first half-hour of the cafe session afterwards is set aside for anyone who wants to come in without buying anything.
https://secondreel.example/listings/the-envelope-house-clover

See you in the stalls,
Albie Morse, listings editor

Second Reel · 26 Wren Passage, London WC1N 3JF

issues.subject: Second Reel · {date}: Three ways to get lost in London
issues.text:
Second Reel · {date}

Three ways to get lost in London

We had two entirely separate listings for a film called East of the Bridge until the print numbers came in. The one on Friday is the river film.

Tuesday at Junction Hall: Borrowed Keys
An estate caretaker accepts an unusually heavy envelope on his last shift. David Pell spent two winters shooting on the same outdoor stair at different times of the day. If you know the version with the blue titles, this one has Pell's original chalk lettering and three additional minutes on the landing. There's no introduction. They plan to start the projector at 19:30 and have the room clear by 21:10.
https://secondreel.example/listings/borrowed-keys-junction

Friday at Low Arch: East of the Bridge
The water looks almost white in the new scan of Mary Cann's 1971 film. A lock worker is trying to walk a borrowed dog from one end of the dock to the other. There are few lines of dialogue and no score in the last reel. This week's ticket includes a 10-minute short about the bridge's signal box, which comes on after the main feature at 21:40.
https://secondreel.example/listings/east-of-the-bridge-low-arch

Sunday at Lantern Rooms: Service Road
We saw an off-air copy of Service Road years ago and were surprised to learn it was shot on film. An overnight road crew takes its breaks in a clubhouse with no working clock. The Lantern's 17:15 slot uses the archive's scan, complete with the tape markings at the reel changes. The place is upstairs, but the lift from the yard is back after two weeks out of service.
https://secondreel.example/listings/service-road-lantern

See you in the stalls,
Albie Morse, listings editor

Second Reel · 26 Wren Passage, London WC1N 3JF

issues.subject: Second Reel · {date}: A western on a wet afternoon
issues.text:
Second Reel · {date}

A western on a wet afternoon

The Clover is doing its early Saturday show again. The cafe around the corner closes between lunch and tea, so bring something if you're staying for the second half of the bill.

Thursday at Low Arch: The Coil
Ada Koenig's 1983 film about a switchboard operator has nearly as much silence as dial tone. In the fourth reel a wire hangs just in front of the camera for twelve seconds. We still argue about whether it was left there on purpose. The arch is showing a subtitled digital edition at 20:00, with a ten-minute introduction from projectionist Ted Marsh about the damaged original negative.
https://secondreel.example/listings/the-coil-low-arch

Saturday at Clover: Three Miles to Elbert
A remarkably small western shot largely along one line of fence. The man selling the cattle gets there first and spends the next hour trying to keep the buyer from seeing what is across the road. The Saturday screening starts at 13:15, with a 20-minute film on women working in the processor's lab to follow. One £10 ticket covers both. Seats are numbered from the screen backwards.
https://secondreel.example/listings/three-miles-to-elbert-clover

Sunday at Junction Hall: Portrait with Pigeons
Local filmmaker Nick Vardy kept his camera in the same kitchen for one summer, pointed at a woman with three baskets of racing pigeons outside her flat. The camera moves once. An excellent short about a laundrette repairman precedes the feature. Doors open at 16:30 and the screening will finish around six. Pay what you can at the trestle table by the entrance to the hall.
https://secondreel.example/listings/portrait-with-pigeons-junction

See you in the stalls,
Albie Morse, listings editor

issues.subject: Second Reel · {date}: An evening in the projection room
issues.text:
Second Reel · {date}

An evening in the projection room

This week's 16mm double is running on Junction Hall's spare machine. The prints are fine. It's the motor they've been coaxing through the summer.

Wednesday at Junction Hall: Dome Keepers
Two short films tracing the end of a public observatory. June Pace's film has a wonderful sequence of the main lens being lowered to the floor on lengths of washing line. The second is by a teenager who shot most of it from the grounds outside. They are showing both at 19:00 and taking questions until 20:20. The stair to the projection room will be open afterwards in small groups.
https://secondreel.example/listings/dome-keepers-junction

Friday at Lantern Rooms: A Minute on Hold
There's a long delay before anyone in this 1992 comedy realises that the call waiting sound is coming from the office next door. We particularly like the set of cardboard headsets in the training room. The hired print is a shade pink throughout and has a few seconds missing at a reel change. The Lantern decided to screen it anyway, in its usual Friday 20:15 slot.
https://secondreel.example/listings/a-minute-on-hold-lantern

Sunday at Clover: Three Small Orbits
Clover's matinee puts Judith Neave's year of evening skies alongside two recent films about watching from the ground. The most recent is eight minutes of shadows crossing a tennis court. The programme runs 73 minutes from 14:00. Notes on the three projection formats will be available on the table outside, with a larger print version at the till. You can see the afternoon's unreserved seats on the listing page.
https://secondreel.example/listings/three-small-orbits-clover

See you in the stalls,
Albie Morse, listings editor

Second Reel · 26 Wren Passage, London WC1N 3JF

issues.subject: Second Reel · {date}: Two doubles and one very short score
issues.text:
Second Reel · {date}

Two doubles and one very short score

The first of the autumn programmes has landed at the Lantern. We're starting with the silent double on Wednesday, because the pianist has written out the cue for the collapsing umbrella.

Wednesday at Lantern Rooms: The Unclaimed Umbrella
Helen Jowett's little comedy about a lost-property counter lasts just seventeen minutes. Pianist Kate Lomas will play the cue she found on the back of a piano part from the film's second run, then accompany another short about a queue outside a pawnshop. Doors are at 18:45. The Lantern moved the piano off the stage so those sitting on the right can see the screen.
https://secondreel.example/listings/the-unclaimed-umbrella-lantern

Friday at Junction Hall: Stairs Up, Stairs Down
Anna Stitt filmed two tenants on opposite sides of a hotel stairwell for Stairs Up, then returned in winter to shoot Stairs Down with the upstairs tenant now minding reception. You'll see the same handrail change colour between films. Both are on 16mm with an interval while the projectionist changes the reel. Come for the 19:15 start, because the inside door is directly next to the screen.
https://secondreel.example/listings/stairs-up-stairs-down-junction

Saturday at Low Arch: A Handful of Slate
Jay Perrott's quarry films were made with a tape recorder held inside a coat and a camera borrowed from the geography department. In the second film you can hear the material sliding a few seconds before you see it move. The archive has cleaned up the tape but left those offsets alone. Both films are showing from digital files at 20:30, with the last train timings posted beside the coat rack.
https://secondreel.example/listings/a-handful-of-slate-low-arch

See you in the stalls,
Albie Morse, listings editor

Second Reel · 26 Wren Passage, London WC1N 3JF
